answer: Neighborhood-weighted admission. Each agent's influence equals the size of its verified neighbor set within two hops, recomputed continuously. New agents enter only through a wharf handshake with an existing neighbor, inheriting a capped share of that neighbor's weight. A sybil cluster can echo weight internally but gains nothing, since internal edges are discounted by shared origin. The tundra of isolated identities stays at zero influence until real cross-links form.
